questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles locking when it moves runner capacity between pools? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A build thread calls RunnerPool.reserve() on a pool while another thread is in the middle of rebalance() involving that pool. What happens to the reserve() call?
choices: It fails immediately with CapacityError because the pool is being modified
It proceeds using the old capacity value, since capacity is read without the lock
It blocks until rebalance() has released that pool's lock, then sees the updated capacity
It acquires the registry guard first and is queued behind the rebalance

questions.prompt: In PoolRegistry.get(), the guard is released before rebalance() takes the pool locks. What is the practical effect of that choice?
choices: Pool lookups never wait on long-running pool operations, but a pool object may be used after the lookup without the guard held
A pool can be removed from the registry while rebalance() holds its lock, corrupting the dict
The registry guard and the pool locks become the same lock
Lookups for different pools are serialized behind each rebalance

questions.prompt: rebalance(src, dst, 5) is called when src has only 3 idle runners. What is the state afterwards?
choices: src.capacity is reduced by 3 and dst.capacity increased by 3
src.capacity is reduced by 5 and in_use is clamped
Both pools' capacities are unchanged, but the locks stay held until the log line runs
Both pools' capacities are unchanged and both locks are released
